memory_update.text: MRVL should remain a reference anchor for AI interconnect because its disclosures span custom AI accelerators, optical DSPs, Ethernet switching, DCI optical modules, AEC and PCIe adjacency.
ALAB is the most direct pure-play mapping to AI fabric plumbing, but current market cap and attention level make it a benchmark rather than an underfollowed discovery candidate.
CRDO remains a direct AEC exposure for AI/ML hyperscale infrastructure; next layers should focus heavily on customer concentration and whether 1.6T adoption is broad or customer-specific.

SMTC is the best underfollowed candidate in this four-name pass because CopperEdge maps directly to lower-power AI data-center copper connectivity while the company is often categorized outside the AI fabric narrative.

Layer 1C should separately test adjacent candidates not included due to the four-name cap: RMBS for CXL/memory-interface chips, APH for high-speed connectors and active/passive interconnects, MTSI for optical/signal-integrity semiconductors, and AAOI for optical transceiver exposure.

node: AI fabric interconnect silicon and board-level connectivity
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for AI fabric interconnect plumbing. The cleanest direct exposures are no longer tiny: Astera Labs and Credo have become large-cap, high-attention pure plays, while Marvell is an obvious reference leader across AI custom silicon, optical DSPs, switching and interconnect. The more underfollowed direct-lane candidate in this pass is Semtech, whose CopperEdge active copper cable redriver/equalizer portfolio maps closely to board- and rack-level AI connectivity but is less commonly framed as an AI fabric chokepoint than GPU, switch, or optical-module leaders. No buy/sell view is implied.
